items.title: Examples of Satisfiable and Unsatisfiable Expressions

source_refs.note: Unnumbered heading Examples of Satisfiable and Unsatisfiable Expressions under 2.7, with the Class Activity, as printed (PDF 30, printed 26).

blocks.text: An example of a satisfiable expression is “P OR Q.” This is true if either P or Q is true. Another example is “P AND Q,” which is true when both P and Q are true. An unsatisfiable expression is “P AND NOT P.” This is never true because P cannot be both true and false. Satisfiable expressions have at least one true outcome, while unsatisfiable expressions have none. Understanding these examples helps in learning logic and problem-solving.

blocks.title: Class Activity
blocks.text: Provide several expressions and ask students to classify them as satisfiable or unsatisfiable.
